preamble: A front mid vowel /e/ in hiatus before another vowel loses its syllabicity and becomes the palatal glide [j]. This yod formation was a major Vulgar Latin change (condemned in the Appendix Probi as 'vinea non vinia') that fed later Romance palatalizations, and the same desyllabification recurs in modern European Portuguese, where unstressed /e/ before a vowel is realized as [j].

examples.note: Appendix Probi: 'uinea non uinia'; the yod later palatalizes the nasal: Italian vigna, French vigne, Spanish viña.
Unstressed /e/ before a stressed vowel is reduced to the glide [j]; cf. Spanish [t̪eˈa.t̪ɾo] with hiatus preserved.
